main_text.p: quæ essent ingeniosæ, animosæ, minimè inertes, corporibus pulchræ, agiles, robustæ, quales in gymnicis certaminibus maximè spectari & cognosci poterant: ut proci virgines nubiles, quas jungere sibi cupiebant, raperent, (invitas an volentes, & jam ante matrimonium pactas, incertum; quanquàm hoc quàm illud magis verosimile:) deinde ut raptam aliquam pronuba abduceret, & caput ejus circumtonderet ad cutem usque, ac virili veste & calceamentis indutam in torum rudem reclinaret, relinqueretque solam sine lumine: ad eam verò sponsus, haudquaquàm ebrius, ac delicatis epulis bene pastus, sed in phiditiis more solito parcè cœnatus sobriusque, latenter & velut furtim ingrederetur, & cingulum sponsæ solveret, & cum eâ sublatâ in lectum genialem se conjiceret: nec diu in complexu ejus moratus, clàm rursum è thalamo egressus dormitum consideret ad juvenes sodales, quibuscum cubare ex lege consueverat: atque hoc non semel tantummodò faceret, sed sæpè ac diu, transfigeretque cum coætaneis suis dies ac noctes, ad sponsam verò itaret verecundè & cautè, quasi præ pudore metuens, ne quis ex familia ingressum egressumque suum perfen-tisceret,

page.notes: The scan shows a small mark in the left margin beside the line "consideret", possibly a reference mark or a stray stain; I could not read it and did not transcribe it. The letters "tabs", "VOV" and "AOA" at the bottom left lie in the margin below the text; they look like show-through or stray marks, not printed text, so I left them out. The printed line "sine lumine" is as shown; "fine" in the scan is the long-s form of "sine" and is transcribed as "sine". Long s is written as plain s throughout.
